findings.title: Read-only group permissions authorize top-level group mutations
findings.body: canManage() accepts either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() relies on this check to authorize both creating groups and moving existing subgroups to the top level. Consequently, an administrator granted only read access to groups can mutate the group hierarchy. This check must require MANAGE, with a regression test confirming that VIEW alone cannot perform either operation.

findings.title: Authorization resource IDs are used as model group IDs
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema names a per-group authorization resource after the GroupModel ID, but the resource has its own independently generated ID. This loop passes the authorization ID to hasPermission(), which looks it up by name, and returns that same authorization ID as a group-membership filter. For example, an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant returns the synthetic resource's ID, so user searches and counts restricted by this set cannot match real memberships. Evaluate and return actual model group IDs, handling the synthetic all-groups resource separately.

findings.title: The member-view scan excludes newly created per-group resources
findings.body: This scan requires Resource.type to be Groups, but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates per-group resources with only a name and scopes; it does not assign their type. Only the synthetic all-groups resource initialized by the schema has that type. An individual VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant therefore contributes no membership filter. User searches paginate all realm users before checking canView(), so permitted members outside the unfiltered page disappear from results. Assign the type to per-group resources or enumerate them through another reliable association.

findings.title: The delegated member-creation fallback remains gated on V1
findings.body: canCreateGroupMembers() returns false unless the V1 ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. With only V2 enabled, an administrator granted the new manage-members and manage-membership scopes on every group in a new user's representation still fails the global Users manage check and receives 403 without evaluating those group permissions. The existing delegated member-creation path needs to admit V2 as well, with coverage for creating a user using group-scoped permissions.

findings.title: Existing V2 realms are not initialized with the Groups schema
findings.body: The fallback assumes an all-groups resource exists, but AdminPermissionsSchema.init() immediately returns when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. A realm initialized before this change contains only the Users and Clients schema resources and lacks the new group-specific scopes. Its Groups lookup therefore returns null, which is passed to the policy lookup and subsequently dereferenced during evaluation; creating group permissions also cannot resolve the missing scopes. Reconcile or migrate existing resource servers before using the new resource type.
